Note::tex_to_text¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signatures¶

Note Note::tex_to_text() const
Note Note::tex_to_text(std::int64_t mode) const

Reduce Authored TeX To Readable Plain Text¶

tex_to_text() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with each cell stripped down from TeX/LaTeX markup to the prose it carries. Use it when the input is already .tex-style content and the downstream step wants plain text — full-text indexing, search snippets, embeddings, summarization, a plain-text export column.

It is the opposite direction from tex_escape: tex_escape protects text so TeX will typeset it verbatim; tex_to_text throws the TeX scaffolding away and keeps the words.

What is removed and what is kept¶

In order, each cell is passed through:

  1. Comments — everything from an unescaped % to end of line.

  2. Preamble — content before \begin{document} and after \end{document} (when those markers are present).

  3. Math — inline ($…$), display (\[…\], $$…$$), and \begin{equation}-style environments are dropped entirely, contents and all.

  4. Text-wrapping commands — \text{…}, \textbf{…}, \textit{…}, \emph{…}, \underline{…}, \texttt{…}, \mathrm{…}, \mathbf{…}, \mathit{…}, \mathsf{…}, \operatorname{…} are replaced by their braced content.

  5. Every other \command — removed. A symbol macro such as \alpha leaves nothing behind; it is not transliterated to α or alpha.

  6. Remaining { and } become spaces; runs of whitespace collapse to one; the cell is trimmed.

Because math and symbol macros are dropped, a cell that is only math becomes empty, and a round trip through tex_escape is lossy (the escapes it adds read as commands here).

mode¶

mode = 0 (the default) applies the pipeline above. mode >= 1 additionally case-folds the recovered text (ASCII lowercase), matching the “sanitize” convention used elsewhere in the library — handy when the output feeds a case-insensitive index or key. Negative values behave like 0.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: Commands And Math¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"Text \\textbf{bold} and $x + y$.", "$only math$"}).tex_to_text())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["Text bold and .", ""]

\textbf{bold} becomes bold; $x + y$ is dropped (the trailing . is prose and stays, and the gap collapses). A math-only cell reduces to empty.

Example 2: Comments And Preamble¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note(
    {"\\documentclass{article}\n% note\n\\begin{document}\nBody \\emph{here}\n\\end{document}"})
    .tex_to_text();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["Body here"]

The class line and the % note comment are gone; only the document body survives, with \emph{here} unwrapped.

Example 3: mode >= 1 Also Case-Folds¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"\\textbf{Hello} World"}).tex_to_text(1))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["hello world"]

Example 4: mode 0 Is The Default¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"\\textbf{Hello} World"}).tex_to_text(0))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["Hello World"]

Example 5: A Scalar — Symbol Macros Vanish¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout,
                   pluss::make_note("\\alpha kept? \\textit{no}").tex_to_text())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"kept? no"

\alpha leaves nothing; \textit{no} unwraps to no.

See Also¶

  • Note::tex_escape: the opposite direction — protect text for TeX.

  • pluss::coden::Note::tex_strip_comments / tex_strip_preamble: run just one stage of the pipeline.

  • Note::nlp_mask_pii: a different “clean this text” pass, keyed to identifiers rather than markup.
